main_text.p: strength of his understanding to define: “ Whetherf the martyrs themselves were in their own persons present at one time in such diverse places, so far distant one from another:” or whether they remaining in a certain place removed from all commerce with the affairs of men here, “ butg praying in general for the necessities of suppliants ;” God by the ministry of his angels did effect these things when, where, and in what manner he pleased, but “ especiallyh at the memorials of the martyrs, because he knew that to be expedient to us for the building of the faith of Christ, for whose confession they did suffer. Thisi matter is higher,” saith he, “ than that it may be touched by me, and more abstruse than that it can be searched into by me: and therefore whether of these two it be, or whether peradventure both of them be, that these things may sometimes be done by the very presence of the martyrs, sometimes by angels taking upon them the person of the martyrs, I dare not define.”

The first of these opinions pleaseth St. Hierome best, who allegeth for proof thereof that place in the Revelation, “ Thesek follow the Lamb, whithersoever he goeth.” Whereupon he inferreth a conclusion, which hath need of a very favourable interpretation: “ Ifl the Lamb be every where, they also that are with the Lamb, must be believed to be every where.” From whom Maximus Taurinensis seemeth not much to differ, when he saith: “ Althoughm
{f} Utrum ipsi per seipsos adsint uno tempore tam diversis locis, et tanta inter se longinquitate discretis, &c. Augustin. de cura pro mortuis, cap. 16. op. tom. 6. pag. 528.
{g} Et tamen generaliter orantibus pro indigentia supplicantium. Ibid.
{h} Maximeque per eorum memorias; quoniam hos novit expedire nobis ad aedificandam fidem Christi, pro cujus illi confessione sunt passi. Ibid.

{i} Res haec altior est, quam ut a me possit attingi, et abstrusior quam ut a me valeat perscrutari: et ideo quid horum duorum sit, an vero fortassis utrumque sit, ut aliquando ista fiant per ipsam praesentiam martyrum, aliquando per angelos suscipientes personam martyrum, definire non audeo. Ibid.
{l} Si agnus ubique: ergo et hi, qui cum agno sunt, ubique esse credendi sunt. Hieronym. advers. Vigilant.
{m} Licet universi sancti ubique sint, et omnibus prosint: specialiter illi tamen pro nobis intervenient, qui et supplicia pertulere pro nobis. Maxim. homil. in natali Taurinorum martyrum..

page.notes: Superscript reference letters in the text are marked as printed; the marginal letters are reproduced in the footnotes. The top-left number is the page number. The text of the last footnote is partly faint and the line ends are uncertain.
